messages:
Maria Chen: Quick heads-up — the sample-app streaming e2e is flaky. Observed out-of-order / duplicated final tokens when auth refresh happens mid-stream.
AJ: Repro steps? which SDK (node/python/browser)? :eyes:
Maria Chen: Node SDK (v0.12.3) in the sample app. Steps:
  1) start a long SSE stream from the hosted API
  2) set short-lived token so refresh runs ~10s in
  3) client does auth-refresh -> we see a 401 then reconnect
  4) client logs show chunks arriving with fragments merged incorrectly and last chunk duplicated
AJ: Ugh. Any logs/snippets?
Maria Chen: Paste of the client log (trimmed):
```
EVENT: data: : {"type":"delta","text":"Hel"
EVENT: data: : {"type":"delta","text":"lo"}
--- auth refresh triggered ---
EVENT: data: : {"type":"delta","text":" world"}
EVENT: data: : [DONE]
```
You can see the "Hel"/"lo" split then a reconnect that sends " world" separately — client ends up assembling "Hello worldworld" in some runs.
Rachel L: Hmm I bet the JS SDK stream parser merges chunks on newline boundaries and our reconnect path doesn't re-sync last-event-id, so fragments get replayed. Python SDK probably trims/handles differently.
Samir Patel: Also check that auth refresh flow doesn't resend the same pending fragment. If the SDK retries the HTTP request without de-dup on the server side, you can double-play fragments.
Maria Chen: We confirmed server logs show the second connection got a partial continuation and the runtime emitted the same last token twice (race between KV cache flush and reconnection).
AJ: Short-term workaround for the sample app: buffer until full event delimiter and dedupe duplicate final tokens on client side. We should push a patch to the node-sdk sample.
Rachel L: I'll open a tiny PR that does two things: 1) hold partial fragments in buffer until an entire JSON message is parsed, and 2) use Last-Event-ID header to prefer newer streams. PR #4321 (draft).
Samir Patel: For infra/runtime — we should make reconnect path include an idempotency token or sequence numbers in the SSE events to make clients robust. Adding a small seq field in events would help ordering guarantees.
infra-bot: deploy/log: runtime patch candidate deployed to canary at 2026-03-21T14:42:01Z (build bld-2026-03-21-7).
AJ: Related DX issue: onboarding docs for streaming apps don't mention auth-refresh pitfalls or recommend pre-warming tokens for long streams. We should add a note and a snippet for pre-signed URLs or refresh hooks.
Maria Chen: Agreed. Also observed parity gap: python-sdk does automatic JSON boundary detection and will drop empty/malformed fragments, whereas node-sdk emitted them as events. We need parity tests in CI.
Rachel L: I'll add a small e2e test that simulates token expiry mid-stream and asserts no duplicated final tokens. That will catch regressions.
Samir Patel: Open question for product: do we want stronger guarantees (at-least-once vs exactly-once ordering) at the runtime level, or keep runtime lean and move to seq ids + client dedupe? Tradeoffs: perf vs complexity.
AJ: Let's take the pragmatic route: seq ids in events (low overhead) + client dedupe. If customers need stricter semantics we can provide a mode.
Maria Chen: Patch + doc + e2e ticketed: I'll create a single epic and link the PR. Thanks — will follow up with the sample-app branch and a small reproduction script.
AJ: Thanks :thumbsup:
Rachel L: Leaving a note: when testing locally, set env STREAM_TOKEN_TTL=30 to force mid-stream refresh. Saves time.
Maria Chen: Good tip. Will ping when PR is ready for review. :rocket:
